questions.question: What is the minimum size of copper conductor allowed for general wiring?
questions.tutor: PEC allows 14 AWG as minimum copper for general branch circuits (except fixtures).

questions.question: What is the maximum overcurrent protection for 14 AWG copper wire?
questions.tutor: 14 AWG copper is rated 15 A maximum overcurrent device.

questions.question: What color is the grounding conductor?
questions.tutor: Grounding conductors must be green, green with yellow stripe, or bare.

questions.question: What is the minimum burial depth for direct burial UF cable under a driveway?
questions.tutor: Direct burial under driveways requires 24 inches cover.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of current-carrying conductors in a 1-inch EMT before derating?
questions.tutor: Derating applies when more than 3 current-carrying conductors are bundled.

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance of service drop conductors over a residential roof?
questions.tutor: Service drop must have at least 3 ft clearance over roof with slope ≥ 4:12.

questions.question: What is the maximum distance between outlet boxes in a residential wall?
questions.tutor: No point along floor line more than 6 ft from an outlet.

questions.question: What is the required height for receptacle outlets above floor in residences?
questions.tutor: Standard height is 15 inches (measured to top of box).

questions.question: What is the minimum size of service entrance for a single-family dwelling of 150 sq m?
questions.tutor: Minimum service for dwelling is 100 A regardless of calculated load.

questions.question: What is the maximum voltage drop for branch circuits?
questions.tutor: PEC recommends max 3% for branch circuits, 5% total (feeder+branch).

questions.question: What type of protection is required for 15A and 20A receptacles in a wet location?
questions.tutor: Wet locations (outdoors, bathrooms, kitchens) require GFCI.

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance for a service head above grade?
questions.tutor: Service head must be at least 10 ft above finished grade.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of quarter bends in a conduit run?
questions.tutor: Maximum is 360 degrees total (four 90° bends).

questions.question: What is the minimum ampacity for a small appliance branch circuit in a kitchen?
questions.tutor: Small appliance circuits must be 20 A rated.

questions.question: How many small appliance branch circuits are required for a residence?
questions.tutor: At least two 20 A small appliance circuits for kitchen, pantry, dining.

questions.question: What is the minimum working space in front of an electrical panel?
questions.tutor: Minimum depth of working space is 30 inches (or width of equipment).

questions.question: What is the required width of working space for electrical equipment?
questions.tutor: Working space width must be at least 30 inches.

questions.question: What is the maximum height of a service disconnect switch?
questions.tutor: Service disconnect handle must not exceed 6 ft 7 inches above floor.

questions.question: What is the minimum size grounding electrode conductor for a 100 A service?
questions.tutor: For 100 A service, min GEC is 8 AWG copper (Table 250.66).

questions.question: What is the required length of a driven ground rod?
questions.tutor: Minimum ground rod length is 8 ft (250.52).

questions.question: What is the maximum resistance of a single ground electrode?
questions.tutor: If resistance >25 ohms, a second electrode must be added.

questions.question: What is the minimum spacing between two ground rods?
questions.tutor: Multiple rods must be at least 6 ft apart (250.53).

questions.question: What is the maximum load on a 15 A branch circuit for non-continuous loads?
questions.tutor: Continuous load max 80% (12A), non-continuous up to 15A.

questions.question: What is the maximum continuous load on a 20 A branch circuit?
questions.tutor: Continuous load max = 80% of rating = 20×0.8=16 A.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of lighting outlets for a residential hallway?
questions.tutor: Hallways of 10 ft or more require at least one lighting outlet.

questions.question: What is the required AFCI protection for residential bedrooms?
questions.tutor: AFCI protection required for all 120V, 15/20A branch circuits in dwelling units.

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance for overhead conductors over public streets?
questions.tutor: Minimum 18 ft over public streets (Table 230.24).

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance for conductors over a residential driveway?
questions.tutor: Minimum 12 ft over residential driveways.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of THHN conductor for a 30 A circuit?
questions.tutor: 30 A circuit requires at least 10 AWG copper.

questions.question: What is the maximum rating of a branch circuit supplying fixed lighting?
questions.tutor: Branch circuit for fixed lighting max 30 A.

questions.question: What is the minimum conductor size for a service neutral for a 200 A dwelling?
questions.tutor: Neutral can be reduced but not smaller than 2 AWG Cu for 200 A service.

questions.question: What is the maximum distance from a pool to a receptacle?
questions.tutor: Receptacles must be at least 20 ft from inside pool wall.

questions.question: What is the required GFCI protection for pool lighting?
questions.tutor: All pool lighting circuits require GFCI protection.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of conductor for a feeder tap?
questions.tutor: Feeder tap conductors must be at least 10 AWG.

questions.question: What is the maximum length of a 10 AWG feeder tap?
questions.tutor: Tap not over 10 ft long if ampacity not less than tap load.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of EGC for a 60 A circuit?
questions.tutor: Table 250.122: 60 A circuit needs 10 AWG Cu EGC.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of disconnecting throws to cut all service power?
questions.tutor: Service can be disconnected by max 6 switches or breakers.

questions.question: What is the minimum clearance for service conductors above a roof?
questions.tutor: Minimum 8 ft clearance over roofs (with exceptions).

questions.question: What is the minimum size of conduit for 2 #12 THHN conductors?
questions.tutor: 1/2 EMT can hold up to 5 #12 THHN (Table C.1).

questions.question: What is the maximum ampacity of 8 AWG THHN copper in a 60°C terminal?
questions.tutor: 8 AWG THHN is 55A at 90°C but limited by terminal rating (60°C = 40A).

questions.question: What is the required number of ground rods if first has 30 ohms resistance?
questions.tutor: If resistance >25 ohms, add a second rod.

questions.question: What is the minimum distance of a wall receptacle from a doorway?
questions.tutor: No specific distance; but no point >6 ft from receptacle.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of main bonding jumper for 400 A service?
questions.tutor: Table 250.66: 400 A service uses 1/0 AWG Cu bonding jumper.

questions.question: What is the maximum voltage drop for feeders?
questions.tutor: Feeder max 2% drop, total including branch max 5%.

questions.question: What is the minimum depth for rigid metal conduit under a driveway?
questions.tutor: RMC requires only 6 inches cover under driveways.

questions.question: What is the required GFCI protection for kitchen countertop receptacles?
questions.tutor: All kitchen countertop receptacles require GFCI protection.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of service entrance for a commercial building with 80 A load?
questions.tutor: Minimum service size for commercial is 100 A (not dwelling).

questions.question: What is the maximum rating of a receptacle on a 15 A individual branch circuit?
questions.tutor: Receptacle rating must not exceed branch circuit rating.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of THWN for a 100 A feeder in a dry location?
questions.tutor: Table 310.16: 2 AWG Cu at 75°C is rated 115 A, sufficient for 100 A.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of 14 AWG conductors in 3/4 EMT?
questions.tutor: 3/4 EMT max fill for #14 THHN is 12 conductors (Chapter 9 Table).

questions.question: What is the atomic number of an element?
choices: Number of electrons in the valence shell
questions.tutor: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus, which defines the element.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.tutor: Electrons are negatively charged particles orbiting the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy the first energy level (n=1)?
questions.tutor: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n². For n=1, 2(1)² = 2 electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following is a noble gas?
questions.tutor: Helium (He) is a noble gas in Group 18, characterized by a full valence shell.

questions.question: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.tutor: A neutral solution has pH = 7, where [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M.

questions.question: What type of bond is formed by the sharing of electrons between atoms?
questions.tutor: Covalent bonds involve sharing of electron pairs between nonmetal atoms.

questions.question: What is the molar mass of water (H₂O)?
How many moles are present in 36 grams of water (H₂O)?
questions.tutor: Moles = mass/molar mass = 36 g / 18 g/mol = 2 mol.

questions.question: Which law states that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant pressure?
questions.tutor: Charles's Law: V ∝ T at constant P and n.

questions.question: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in most compounds?
questions.tutor: Oxygen typically has an oxidation state of -2, except in peroxides (-1) and OF₂ (+2).

questions.question: What is the balanced equation for the combustion of methane (CH₄)?
questions.tutor: Balanced: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?
questions.topic: General Chemistry - Physical vs Chemical Change
questions.tutor: Melting of ice is a phase change (solid to liquid) without changing chemical composition.

questions.question: What is the electron configuration of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.tutor: Na (Z=11): 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹.

questions.question: What is the concentration in ppm of a solution containing 0.005 g of solute in 1 kg of solvent?
questions.tutor: ppm = (mass of solute / mass of solution) × 10⁶ = (0.005/1000)×10⁶ = 5 ppm.

questions.question: Which of the following is a strong electrolyte?
questions.tutor: NaCl dissociates completely into ions in water, making it a strong electrolyte.

questions.question: A radioactive isotope decays from 100 g to 12.5 g in 3 half-lives. What is the half-life in terms of the total time T?
questions.tutor: After 3 half-lives, remaining = initial × (1/2)³ = 12.5 g. Half-life = total time T / 3.

questions.question: What is the Lewis structure for carbon dioxide (CO₂)?
questions.tutor: CO₂ has two double bonds: O=C=O, with carbon as central atom.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 M HCl solution?
Which of the following is a property of acids?
questions.tutor: Acids turn blue litmus paper red. Bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.question: What is the wavelength region of light emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n=3 to n=2?
questions.tutor: The transition n=3 to n=2 emits visible red light (Balmer series, 656 nm).

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of:
questions.tutor: Newton's first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion unless acted upon by a net external force. This is the law of inertia.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.tutor: The Newton (N) is the SI unit of force, defined as 1 kg·m/s².

questions.question: A 2 kg object is moving with a velocity of 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
What is the acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface approximately?
questions.tutor: Standard acceleration due to gravity g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (or 9.81 m/s²).

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.tutor: Mass has magnitude only; velocity, force, and displacement have both magnitude and direction (vectors).

questions.question: Ohm's law states the relationship between:
questions.tutor: Ohm's Law: V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.

questions.question: A 10 Ω resistor carries a current of 2 A. What is the voltage across it?
What is the frequency of a wave with period 0.02 seconds?
The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.tutor: The speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?
What is the work done when a force of 10 N moves an object 5 m in the direction of the force?
What is the principle of conservation of energy?
choices: Energy can be created but not destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
Energy is always lost as heat
questions.tutor: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another.

questions.question: A 5 kg object is lifted 2 meters above the ground. What is its gravitational potential energy?
questions.tutor: PE = mgh = 5 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 2 m = 98 J.

questions.question: What is the momentum of a 10 kg object moving at 3 m/s?
questions.tutor: p = mv = 10 kg × 3 m/s = 30 kg·m/s.

questions.question: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another is called:
questions.tutor: Refraction is the bending of light due to a change in speed when passing between different media.

questions.question: What is the efficiency of a machine that does 200 J of useful work from 500 J of input energy?
questions.tutor: Efficiency = (useful output / input) × 100% = (200/500)×100% = 40%.

questions.question: What is the resonant frequency of an LC circuit with L = 0.1 H and C = 10 μF?
Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.tutor: Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ = 4 + 6 = 10 Ω.

questions.question: What is the image distance for an object placed at the center of curvature of a concave mirror?
questions.tutor: For a concave mirror, when object is at C, image is also at C, real, inverted, and same size.

questions.question: A force of 50 N is applied to a spring with spring constant 200 N/m. What is the extension?
questions.tutor: Hooke's Law: F = kx → x = F/k = 50/200 = 0.25 m.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.tutor: CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the primary component that executes instructions in a computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a volatile memory?
questions.tutor: RAM (Random Access Memory) loses its data when power is turned off, making it volatile.

questions.question: What is the binary equivalent of the decimal number 13?
Which programming language is primarily used for artificial intelligence and machine learning?
questions.tutor: Python is widely used in AI/ML due to libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.tutor: HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Which operator is used for integer division in Python?
questions.tutor: // is floor division operator in Python, returning the integer quotient.

questions.question: What is the output of 2 ** 3 in Python?
questions.tutor: ** is the exponentiation operator. 2³ = 8.

questions.question: What is the decimal equivalent of hexadecimal number 1A?
Which of the following is a non-volatile memory?
questions.tutor: ROM (Read-Only Memory) retains data even when power is off.

questions.question: What is the correct way to write a comment in C language?
questions.tutor: C supports single-line comments (//) and multi-line comments (/* */).

questions.question: What does an AND gate output?
choices: 1 if at least one input is 1
questions.tutor: AND gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.

questions.question: What is the output of the Boolean expression A·(A+B)?
questions.tutor: A·(A+B) = A·A + A·B = A + AB = A(1+B) = A.

questions.question: Which data structure follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle?
questions.tutor: Stack follows LIFO: last element pushed is the first popped.

questions.question: What is the function of an operating system?
questions.tutor: OS manages hardware, software, processes, memory, and provides user interface.

questions.question: What is the octal equivalent of binary 101101?
Which loop guarantees at least one execution in C?
questions.tutor: do-while loop executes the body first, then checks condition, ensuring at least one iteration.

questions.question: What does SQL stand for?
questions.tutor: SQL is used to manage and query relational databases.

questions.question: What is the value of the binary number 1111 in decimal?
Which of the following is a high-level programming language?
questions.tutor: Python is a high-level language; assembly and machine code are low-level.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a compiler?
choices: Converts high-level code to machine code
questions.tutor: A compiler translates entire high-level source code into machine code before execution.

questions.question: What is the primary constituent of mild steel?
questions.tutor: Mild steel is primarily iron (Fe) with small amounts of carbon (0.05-0.25%) and other elements.

questions.question: What is the property of a material to absorb energy and plastically deform without fracturing?
questions.tutor: Toughness is the ability to absorb energy and deform plastically before fracture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-ferrous metal?
questions.tutor: Copper is a non-ferrous metal (contains no significant iron). Cast iron and steel are ferrous.

questions.question: What does the modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus) measure?
questions.tutor: Young's modulus (E) measures a material's stiffness or resistance to elastic deformation.

questions.question: What is the approximate carbon content of cast iron?
questions.tutor: Cast iron contains 2-4% carbon, making it hard but brittle.

questions.question: Which of the following materials is a good electrical conductor?
questions.tutor: Copper has high electrical conductivity, widely used in wires and cables.

questions.question: What is the process of heating and cooling metals to alter their physical properties?
questions.tutor: Heat treatment processes like annealing, quenching, and tempering modify metal properties.

questions.question: What is the main alloying element in stainless steel?
questions.tutor: Chromium (at least 10.5%) provides corrosion resistance in stainless steel.

questions.question: What is the unit of electrical resistivity?
questions.tutor: Electrical resistivity is measured in ohm-meters (Ω·m).

questions.question: Which type of bond is characteristic of metals?
questions.tutor: Metallic bonds involve a 'sea' of delocalized electrons around positive metal ions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of annealing in metals?
questions.tutor: Annealing softens metals, reduces internal stress, and improves ductility.

questions.question: Which of the following is a thermosetting polymer?
questions.tutor: Bakelite is thermosetting (irreversibly hardens when heated). Polyethylene and PVC are thermoplastics.

questions.question: What is the Poisson's ratio of a perfectly incompressible material?
questions.tutor: Poisson's ratio ν = 0.5 for perfectly incompressible materials (e.g., rubber).

questions.question: What is the purpose of adding carbon to iron?
questions.tutor: Carbon increases hardness and strength but reduces ductility in steel.

questions.question: What is the most common crystal structure for metals?
questions.tutor: Common metal structures: BCC (iron at room temp), FCC (aluminum, copper), HCP (zinc).

questions.question: Which of the following is a ceramic material?
questions.tutor: Alumina is a ceramic; brass is metal, polycarbonate is polymer, carbon steel is metal.

questions.question: What is the difference between hardness and toughness?
choices: Hardness resists scratching; toughness resists impact
questions.tutor: Hardness resists indentation/scratching; toughness resists fracture under impact.

questions.question: What does the term 'creep' refer to in materials?
choices: Time-dependent plastic deformation under constant stress
questions.tutor: Creep is slow, continuous deformation under constant load, especially at high temperatures.

questions.question: What is the purpose of galvanizing steel?
questions.tutor: Galvanizing applies a zinc coating to steel to prevent rusting (sacrificial protection).

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest thermal conductivity?
questions.tutor: Copper has very high thermal conductivity (≈400 W/m·K), higher than aluminum and steel.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.tutor: The Newton (N) is the SI unit of force, defined as 1 kg·m/s².

questions.question: What is the sum of all forces acting on a body in equilibrium?
questions.tutor: For a body in equilibrium, the net force (vector sum) must be zero: ΣF = 0.

questions.question: A 10 kg mass is suspended by a rope. What is the tension in the rope (g = 9.8 m/s²)?
questions.tutor: Tension = weight = mg = 10 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 98 N.

questions.question: What is the moment of a force?
questions.tutor: Moment (torque) = Force × perpendicular distance from pivot point.

questions.question: A force of 50 N is applied perpendicular to a wrench handle 0.3 m long. What is the torque?
What is the condition for translational equilibrium?
questions.tutor: Translational equilibrium requires net force = 0 (ΣF = 0).

questions.question: What is the condition for rotational equilibrium?
questions.tutor: Rotational equilibrium requires net moment = 0 (ΣM = 0).

questions.question: A 200 N weight is placed 2 m from the left end of a 5 m uniform beam. Where must the fulcrum be for balance?
questions.tutor: Beam weight acts at center, so both beam weight and load position affect fulcrum location.

questions.question: What is the efficiency of an ideal machine?
questions.tutor: An ideal machine has 100% efficiency (no friction losses).

questions.question: Which of Newton's laws states that action and reaction are equal and opposite?
questions.tutor: Newton's third law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: A car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What is the average acceleration?
What is the frictional force on a 10 kg box on a horizontal surface with μ = 0.4 (g=9.8 m/s²)?
What is the mechanical advantage of a lever with effort arm 4 m and load arm 1 m?
questions.tutor: MA = effort arm / load arm = 4/1 = 4.

questions.question: What is the center of gravity of a uniform rod?
questions.tutor: For a uniform rod, the center of gravity is at its geometric center (midpoint).

questions.question: A 5 kg block is pulled with 20 N force on a frictionless surface. What is its acceleration?
questions.tutor: a = F/m = 20 N / 5 kg = 4 m/s² (Newton's second law).

questions.question: What is the resultant of two perpendicular forces of 3 N and 4 N?
What is the principle of moments?
choices: Sum of clockwise moments = Sum of anticlockwise moments
questions.tutor: The principle of moments states that for equilibrium, clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.

questions.question: A ladder rests against a wall. What forces act at the contact point with the wall?
questions.tutor: Wall exerts both normal force (perpendicular) and friction (parallel) to prevent slipping.

questions.question: What is the slope of a velocity-time graph?
questions.tutor: The slope of velocity-time graph gives acceleration (a = dv/dt).

questions.question: What is the area under a force-displacement graph?
questions.tutor: Work done = ∫F·dx, which is the area under force-displacement curve.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of dynamic viscosity?
questions.tutor: Dynamic viscosity μ is measured in Pascal-seconds (Pa·s) or N·s/m².

questions.question: What is the pressure at a depth of 10 m in water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²) assuming atmospheric pressure is neglected?
Which principle explains the buoyant force on a submerged object?
questions.tutor: Archimedes' principle: buoyant force equals weight of displaced fluid.

questions.question: What is the continuity equation in fluid mechanics?
choices: P₁ + ½ρv₁² + ρgh₁ = P₂ + ½ρv₂² + ρgh₂
questions.tutor: Continuity equation: Q = A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (incompressible flow).

questions.question: What is the Reynolds number used to determine?
questions.tutor: Reynolds number Re = ρvD/μ determines laminar (Re<2000) or turbulent (Re>4000) flow.

questions.question: What does Pascal's principle state?
choices: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished
Buoyant force equals weight of displaced fluid
questions.tutor: Pascal's principle: pressure change in an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally throughout.

questions.question: What is the specific gravity of a fluid with density 800 kg/m³? (ρ_water = 1000 kg/m³)
questions.tutor: SG = ρ_fluid / ρ_water = 800/1000 = 0.8.

questions.question: What is the kinematic viscosity ν if μ = 0.001 Pa·s and ρ = 1000 kg/m³?
What is the pressure head equivalent to 50 kPa in water? (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g=9.8 m/s²)
Which flow meter operates on the principle of Bernoulli's equation?
questions.tutor: Venturi meter uses pressure difference (Bernoulli) to measure flow rate.

questions.question: What is the force on a 2 m² gate submerged vertically in water with its top at the surface? (ρ=1000 kg/m³, g=9.8 m/s²)
questions.tutor: F = ρg × h_c × A = 1000×9.8×(1)×2 = 19,600 N (h_c is centroid depth).

questions.question: What does Bernoulli's equation assume?
choices: Steady, incompressible, inviscid flow along a streamline
questions.tutor: Bernoulli assumes steady, incompressible, frictionless flow along a streamline.

questions.question: What is the hydraulic grade line (HGL)?
questions.tutor: HGL = pressure head + elevation head = P/ρg + z.

questions.question: What is the flow rate in a pipe of diameter 0.2 m if average velocity is 3 m/s?
What is the difference between absolute pressure and gauge pressure?
questions.tutor: Absolute pressure = gauge pressure + atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: What is the Darcy-Weisbach equation used for?
choices: Calculating head loss due to friction in pipes
questions.tutor: Darcy-Weisbach: h_f = f × (L/D) × (v²/2g) for friction head loss.

questions.question: What does the Moody chart provide?
choices: Friction factor f as function of Re and ε/D
questions.tutor: Moody chart gives Darcy friction factor f for pipe flow based on Re and relative roughness.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a pitot tube?
questions.tutor: Pitot tube measures stagnation pressure to compute local velocity via Bernoulli.

questions.question: What is the definition of specific weight?
questions.tutor: Specific weight γ = ρg = weight/volume (N/m³).

questions.question: What happens to fluid velocity in a converging section of a pipe?
questions.tutor: By continuity A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, when area decreases, velocity increases.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of stress?
questions.tutor: Stress is force per unit area, measured in Pascals (Pa) or N/m².

questions.question: What is the definition of strain?
questions.tutor: Strain ε = ΔL / L₀, a dimensionless measure of deformation.

questions.question: Hooke's law states that stress is proportional to strain within the:
questions.tutor: Hooke's law: σ = Eε, valid within the elastic limit where deformation is reversible.

questions.question: A steel rod of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 100 mm² is subjected to a tensile force of 20 kN. What is the stress? (1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m²)
What is Young's modulus a measure of?
questions.tutor: Young's modulus E = σ/ε, representing material stiffness or resistance to elastic deformation.

questions.question: What is the bending moment at the fixed end of a cantilever beam with a point load P at the free end?
questions.tutor: For cantilever with end load, maximum moment at fixed end M = P × L.

questions.question: What is the formula for the deflection of a simply supported beam with a central point load?
questions.tutor: δ_max = PL³/(48EI) for simply supported beam with central point load.

questions.question: What is the Poisson's ratio of a material?
choices: Negative ratio of lateral strain to axial strain
Positive ratio of lateral strain to axial strain
questions.tutor: Poisson's ratio ν = - (lateral strain)/(axial strain), typically 0.25-0.35 for metals.

questions.question: What is the maximum shear stress in a solid circular shaft under torsion?
questions.tutor: τ_max = T×r/J occurs at outer surface (r = radius).

questions.question: What is the polar moment of inertia for a solid circular shaft of diameter d?
questions.tutor: J = πd⁴/32 for solid circular shaft (polar moment).

questions.question: A force of 5000 N is applied to a rod of diameter 10 mm. What is the tensile stress?
What is the factor of safety?
questions.topic: Strength of Materials - Factor of Safety
questions.tutor: FOS = Ultimate strength / Allowable working stress (or yield/working).

questions.question: What is the neutral axis in a beam?
choices: Axis where bending stress is zero
questions.tutor: Neutral axis experiences zero longitudinal stress under pure bending.

questions.question: What is the section modulus Z for a rectangular beam of width b and depth h?
What is the maximum bending stress formula for a beam?
questions.tutor: Bending stress σ = M×c / I, where c is distance from neutral axis to outer fiber.

questions.question: What is the thermal stress in a rod fixed at both ends when temperature increases by ΔT?
questions.tutor: Thermal stress σ = EαΔT when expansion is fully constrained.

questions.question: What is the shear stress formula for a circular shaft in torsion?
questions.tutor: Shear stress τ = T×r / J, where T = torque, r = radius, J = polar moment.

questions.question: What is the modulus of rigidity G?
questions.tutor: G = τ/γ (shear stress over shear strain), also called shear modulus.

questions.question: What is the relationship between E, G, and ν?
questions.tutor: G = E / [2(1+ν)] relates Young's modulus, shear modulus, and Poisson's ratio.

questions.question: What is the endurance limit of a material?
choices: Maximum stress for infinite fatigue life
questions.tutor: Endurance limit is the stress below which material can withstand infinite cycles without failure.

questions.question: What is the zeroth law of thermodynamics?
choices: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
If two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other
Entropy of an isolated system increases
Heat cannot be completely converted into work
questions.tutor: Zeroth law establishes the concept of temperature and thermal equilibrium.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of temperature?
questions.tutor: Kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.question: What is the first law of thermodynamics?
choices: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
Heat flows from hot to cold
Pressure and volume are inversely related
questions.tutor: First law: ΔU = Q - W, energy conservation in thermodynamic systems.

questions.question: What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between 500 K and 300 K?
What does the second law of thermodynamics state about entropy?
choices: Entropy of an isolated system always increases or remains constant
Entropy is zero at absolute zero
questions.tutor: Second law: ΔS ≥ 0 for isolated systems (entropy never decreases).

questions.question: What is an isothermal process?
questions.tutor: Isothermal process occurs at constant temperature (ΔT = 0).

questions.question: What is the work done in an isobaric process?
questions.tutor: For isobaric (constant pressure), W = P(V₂ - V₁) = PΔV.

questions.question: What is an adiabatic process?
questions.tutor: Adiabatic process: Q = 0, no heat exchange with surroundings.

questions.question: What is the specific gas constant R for air? (R_universal = 8.314 kJ/kmol·K, M_air = 28.97 kg/kmol)
questions.tutor: R = R_universal / M = 8.314 / 28.97 = 0.287 kJ/kg·K.

questions.question: What is the triple point of water?
questions.tutor: Triple point of water is 0.01°C (273.16 K) at 611.2 Pa, where ice, liquid, vapor coexist.

questions.question: What is the heat required to change 1 kg of water at 100°C to steam at 100°C? (latent heat of vaporization = 2257 kJ/kg)
questions.tutor: Q = m × h_fg = 1 kg × 2257 kJ/kg = 2257 kJ.

questions.question: What is the coefficient of performance (COP) of a refrigerator?
questions.tutor: COP_R = Q_c / W_net (heat removed from cold reservoir divided by work input).

questions.question: What is an isentropic process?
questions.tutor: Isentropic process: ΔS = 0 (reversible and adiabatic).

questions.question: What is the thermal efficiency of a heat engine?
questions.tutor: η = W_net / Q_in = (Q_in - Q_out)/Q_in.

questions.question: What is absolute zero in Celsius?
questions.tutor: Absolute zero is 0 K = -273.15°C, theoretically lowest possible temperature.

questions.question: What is the work done in a cycle?
choices: Net area enclosed in PV diagram
questions.tutor: Net work for a cycle equals area enclosed by the path on PV diagram.

questions.question: What is the specific heat capacity at constant pressure (cp) for an ideal gas related to cv?
questions.tutor: For ideal gas, cp - cv = R (specific gas constant).

questions.question: What is the ratio of specific heats γ for a diatomic gas like air?
questions.tutor: γ = cp/cv ≈ 1.4 for diatomic gases (air, N₂, O₂).

questions.question: What is a throttling process?
questions.tutor: Throttling (Joule-Thomson) is isenthalpic: h₁ = h₂, pressure drops.

questions.question: What is the entropy change for a reversible isothermal process?
questions.tutor: For reversible isothermal, ΔS = Q_rev / T.

questions.question: What law created the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)?
questions.tutor: RA 8981 (PRC Modernization Act) reorganized and strengthened the PRC.

questions.question: What is the implementing body of RA 7920?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 (New Electrical Engineering Law) is implemented by the Board of Electrical Engineering under PRC.

questions.question: What is the official term of a Board of Electrical Engineering member?
questions.tutor: BOE members serve a term of 3 years under RA 7920.

questions.question: How many members compose the Board of Electrical Engineering?
questions.tutor: The BOE has 3 members: a Chairman and 2 members.

questions.question: What is the required number of years of practice before one can be appointed to the BOE?
questions.tutor: BOE appointees must have at least 10 years of active EE practice.

questions.question: What RA is known as the 'Electrical Engineering Law'?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 is the Philippine Electrical Engineering Law, enacted in 1995.

questions.question: What law requires a Professional Identification Card (PIC) from PRC?
questions.tutor: RA 8981 mandates the issuance of PRC ID cards for registered professionals.

questions.question: What is the Continuing Professional Development (CPD) law?
questions.tutor: RA 10912 is the CPD Act of 2016, requiring CPD units for license renewal.

questions.question: How many CPD units are required for electrical engineers per renewal cycle?
questions.tutor: PRC requires 45 CPD units for EEs every 3-year renewal cycle.

questions.question: What law penalizes unethical practices and graft in government?
questions.tutor: RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) and RA 6713 (Code of Conduct for Public Officials).

questions.question: What is the maximum penalty for practicing EE without a valid license?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 penalizes unlicensed practice with fine up to P100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.

questions.question: What is the lowest passing grade for a subject in the REE board exam?
questions.tutor: No subject grade below 50%, and average of all subjects at least 70%.

questions.question: What is the required average passing grade for REE board exam?
questions.tutor: General average of 70% with no subject below 50%.

questions.question: What is the validity period of a Professional Electrical Engineer (PEE) certificate?
questions.tutor: PEE certificate, like other professional licenses, is valid for 3 years.

questions.question: What PD created the PRC originally?
questions.tutor: PD 223 (1973) created the Professional Regulation Commission.

questions.question: Who appoints the members of the Board of Electrical Engineering?
questions.tutor: BOE members are appointed by the President of the Philippines upon PRC recommendation.

questions.question: What law mandates the use of Filipino technical terms in engineering?
questions.tutor: No specific law mandates exclusively Filipino technical terms; English remains standard.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of RA 9184?
questions.tutor: RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act) governs public bidding and contracts.

questions.question: What is the maximum CPD units that can be earned from self-directed learning?
questions.tutor: PRC allows max 5 CPD units from self-directed learning per renewal period.

questions.question: What law requires electrical plans to be signed by a PEE?
questions.tutor: PD 1096 (NBC) and RA 7920 both require licensed PEE to sign electrical plans for large installations.

questions.question: What is the Code of Ethics for Electrical Engineers embodied in?
questions.tutor: PRC Resolution and IIEE Code of Ethics govern EE professional conduct.

questions.question: What law is known as the 'National Building Code'?
questions.tutor: PD 1096 (1977) is the National Building Code of the Philippines.

questions.question: What law is known as the 'Fire Code of the Philippines'?
questions.tutor: RA 9514 (2008) replaced PD 1185 as the Fire Code of the Philippines.

questions.question: What is the minimum percentage of Filipino participation in engineering consultancy under RA 9184?
questions.tutor: RA 9184 requires at least 60% Filipino equity for consultancy services.

questions.question: What law mandates EE as a profession requiring state regulation?
questions.tutor: 1987 Constitution Article II, Section 14 mandates state regulation of professions.

questions.question: What is the penalty for impersonating a registered EE?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 penalizes impersonation with fine and imprisonment.

questions.question: Who may file a complaint against a registered EE?
questions.tutor: Any person may file a verified complaint before the BOE.

questions.question: What is the maximum fine for violating RA 7920?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 Section 46 imposes fine up to P100,000.

questions.question: What is the maximum imprisonment term under RA 7920?
questions.tutor: Imprisonment up to 2 years for violations of RA 7920.

questions.question: What law created the IIEE as a professional organization?
questions.tutor: IIEE is a private organization; RA 7920 recognizes it as the accredited professional organization (APO).

questions.question: What is the official journal of the PRC?
questions.tutor: PRC publishes The Professional Regulation Commission Journal.

questions.question: What is the requirement for REE license renewal without CPD?
questions.tutor: CPD units are mandatory for license renewal under RA 10912.

questions.question: What is the validity of a Special Professional License (SPL)?
questions.tutor: SPL for foreign EEs is valid for 1 year, renewable.

questions.question: Who issues the Certificate of Registration for EEs?
questions.tutor: PRC Commissioner issues Certificate of Registration upon BOE recommendation.

questions.question: What law is known as the 'Philippine Electrical Code'?
questions.tutor: PEC is part of the implementing rules of RA 7920, not a separate law.

questions.question: What is the required number of years to become a PEE?
questions.tutor: At least 7 years of EE practice required for PEE eligibility.

questions.question: What is the passing rate target per REE board exam?
questions.tutor: No fixed passing rate; it depends on exam difficulty and candidate performance.

questions.question: What government agency oversees the BOE?
questions.tutor: PRC has administrative supervision over all BOEs including Electrical Engineering.

questions.question: What law mandates the use of English as medium of instruction in engineering?
questions.tutor: No law mandates English; it's standard practice from CHED policies.

questions.question: What is the effect of non-renewal of license for 3 consecutive cycles?
questions.tutor: PRC may require re-examination if license expired for 3 cycles (9 years).

questions.question: What law provides for professional civil service eligibility for licensed EEs?
questions.tutor: PD 1080 grants civil service eligibility to board passers.

questions.question: What is the requirement for signing electrical permits for low-voltage installations?
questions.tutor: REE can sign for low-voltage (up to 600V), PEE for higher voltages.

questions.question: What law punishes sexual harassment in the workplace including engineering firms?
questions.tutor: RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995).

questions.question: What law protects intellectual property of engineering designs?
questions.tutor: RA 8293 (IP Code) amended by RA 10372 protects copyrights and patents.

questions.question: What law mandates data privacy in engineering records?
questions.tutor: RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012) protects personal information.

questions.question: What is the minimum passing score per subject in REE board?
questions.tutor: No subject grade below 50% as per BOE resolution.

questions.question: What law provides for mandatory CPD for all professionals?
questions.tutor: RA 10912 (CPD Act of 2016) makes CPD mandatory for all PRC-regulated professions.

questions.question: What is the supervising agency for CPD implementation?
questions.tutor: PRC through the CPD Council implements RA 10912.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of years a license may be suspended?
questions.tutor: BOE may suspend license for up to 3 years under RA 7920.

questions.question: What law mandates the use of renewable energy in the Philippines?
questions.tutor: RA 9513 (Renewable Energy Act of 2008) promotes RE development.

questions.question: What is the time value of money?
choices: Money has same value over time
questions.tutor: Money today is worth more than same amount in future due to earning potential.

questions.question: What is the formula for simple interest?
questions.tutor: Simple interest: I = Principal × rate × time.

questions.question: What is compound interest?
questions.tutor: Compound interest earns interest on both principal and prior interest.

questions.question: What is the future worth of P10,000 after 3 years at 10% compound interest?
What is present worth factor (P/F)?
questions.tutor: (P/F,i,n) = 1/(1+i)^n to find present given future.

questions.question: What is the annual worth of a project?
questions.tutor: Annual Worth (AW) converts all cash flows to equivalent uniform annual amounts.

questions.question: What is the payback period?
questions.tutor: Payback period is time needed to recoup initial investment from cash inflows.

questions.question: What is the formula for Capital Recovery Factor (CRF)?
What is the effective interest rate for 12% compounded monthly?
What does IRR stand for?
questions.tutor: IRR is discount rate where NPV = 0.

questions.question: A project requires P100,000 investment and returns P30,000/year for 5 years. What is the simple payback?
questions.tutor: Payback = Investment / Annual return = 100,000/30,000 = 3.33 years.

questions.question: What is the sinking fund factor (A/F)?
What is depreciation?
choices: Decrease in asset value over time
questions.tutor: Depreciation allocates cost of asset over its useful life.

questions.question: What is straight line depreciation annual rate?
questions.tutor: SL = (Initial Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life.

questions.question: What is the present worth of a perpetuity of P10,000/year at 8%?
What is the benefit-cost ratio (BCR)?
choices: Present worth of benefits / Present worth of costs
questions.tutor: BCR = PV(Benefits) / PV(Costs). Project acceptable if BCR ≥ 1.

questions.question: What does MARR stand for?
questions.tutor: MARR is the minimum acceptable return on an investment.

questions.question: What is the capitalized cost of an asset?
choices: Initial cost + present worth of infinite renewals
questions.tutor: CC = First cost + (Annual cost / i) for perpetual projects.

questions.question: What is salvage value?
choices: Estimated value at end of useful life
questions.tutor: Salvage value is residual worth after asset's useful life.

questions.question: What is the decision rule for NPV?
questions.tutor: Positive NPV means project exceeds required return.

questions.question: What is the primary function of management?
questions.tutor: Management functions include planning, organizing, staffing, directing, and controlling.

questions.question: Who is considered the father of scientific management?
questions.tutor: Frederick Taylor pioneered scientific management and time-motion studies.

questions.question: What does SWOT analysis stand for?
questions.tutor: SWOT analyzes internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats.

questions.question: What is the span of control?
choices: Number of subordinates a manager supervises
questions.tutor: Span of control refers to how many direct reports a manager has.

questions.question: What is a Gantt chart used for?
questions.tutor: Gantt charts visually show task durations and dependencies over time.

questions.question: What is the critical path in a project network?
questions.tutor: Critical path has zero slack; any delay extends project completion.

questions.question: What does PERT stand for?
questions.tutor: PERT uses three time estimates (optimistic, pessimistic, most likely) for uncertain tasks.

questions.question: What is Maslow's hierarchy top need?
questions.tutor: Maslow's pyramid: physiological, safety, love, esteem, self-actualization.

questions.question: Who proposed Theory X and Theory Y?
questions.tutor: Theory X assumes workers are lazy; Theory Y assumes they are self-motivated.

questions.question: What is the break-even point?
questions.tutor: Break-even is where no profit or loss occurs.

questions.question: What is delegation of authority?
questions.tutor: Delegation transfers authority and responsibility to subordinates.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of quality control?
questions.tutor: QC checks products against specifications to maintain quality.

questions.question: What does PDCA cycle stand for?
questions.tutor: PDCA (Deming cycle) is for continuous process improvement.

questions.question: What is the difference between leader and manager?
questions.tutor: Leaders focus on vision and motivation; managers focus on processes and control.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of staffing?
questions.tutor: Staffing involves recruitment, selection, training, and development of employees.

questions.question: What is the formula for labor productivity?
questions.tutor: Labor productivity measures output per unit of labor input.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a feasibility study?
questions.tutor: Feasibility studies assess technical, economic, legal, and operational viability.

questions.question: What is unity of command principle?
choices: Each employee reports to one boss
questions.tutor: Unity of command avoids conflicting instructions from multiple supervisors.

questions.question: What is the primary role of an engineering manager?
questions.tutor: Engineering managers blend technical expertise with management skills.

questions.question: What does KPI stand for?
questions.tutor: KPIs measure how effectively an organization achieves key objectives.

questions.question: What is the primary duty of an electrical engineer according to the Code of Ethics?
questions.tutor: The paramount duty is to protect public safety, health, and welfare.

questions.question: Can an engineer advertise their services in a self-laudatory manner?
questions.tutor: Self-praise or misleading advertising is considered unprofessional.

questions.question: What should an engineer do if they discover a colleague's unethical act?
questions.tutor: Engineers have a duty to report ethical violations to the Board or PRC.

questions.question: May an engineer sign plans not prepared under their supervision?
questions.tutor: Engineers sign only work they personally supervised or reviewed.

questions.question: What is conflict of interest?
questions.tutor: Conflict of interest arises when personal gain influences professional judgment.

questions.question: Can an engineer accept commissions from contractors on projects they supervise?
questions.tutor: Accepting kickbacks or hidden commissions is strictly prohibited.

questions.question: What is the engineer's duty regarding confidential information?
questions.tutor: Engineers must safeguard client's confidential business or technical information.

questions.question: May an engineer bid against another engineer using the same original design?
questions.tutor: Using another's design without compensation is unfair competition.

questions.question: What should an engineer do if a project violates safety codes?
questions.tutor: Engineers must not approve any plan or work violating safety laws.

questions.question: Can an engineer serve two clients with competing interests?
questions.tutor: Simultaneous service to competing clients requires informed consent from both.

questions.question: What is the penalty for practicing EE without a valid license?
questions.tutor: RA 7920 imposes fine up to P100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.

questions.question: May an engineer use their position to obtain personal favors?
questions.tutor: Engineers must not use professional position for personal gain.

questions.question: What is the engineer's obligation regarding continuing education?
questions.tutor: RA 10912 mandates CPD units for license renewal to maintain competence.

questions.question: Can an engineer publicly criticize another engineer's work?
choices: No, except with factual basis and proper forum
questions.tutor: Criticism must be constructive, factual, and through proper professional channels.

questions.question: What should an engineer do if offered a bribe?
questions.tutor: Bribery is unethical and illegal; must be refused and reported.

questions.question: May an engineer sign plans for a project they didn't design?
choices: Only if they review and accept responsibility
questions.tutor: Engineers may sign after thorough review and assuming full responsibility.

questions.question: What is the engineer's duty to the environment?
questions.tutor: Engineers must promote sustainable development and environmental protection.

questions.question: Can an engineer claim credit for work done by others?
questions.tutor: Credit must be given to those who actually performed the work.

questions.question: What is the IIEE's role in ethics enforcement?
questions.tutor: IIEE investigates complaints and recommends disciplinary action to BOE.

questions.question: What does 'primum non nocere' mean in engineering ethics?
questions.tutor: The primary ethical guideline is to avoid causing harm to public.
